newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Feb 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Feb 7.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Friday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal:

* Visa USA Inc and MasterCard International face a possible antitrust challenge by the Justice Department involving their rules barring member banks from issuing American Express and Discover cards, people close to the matter say.
* A blunder by the National Association of Securities Dealers caused as many as 20,000 pieces of regulatory data on the nation's stockbrokers to be purged.
* Tele-Communications International Chairman John Malone is expected to step aside as president. His top choice for the post is cable veteran Leo Hindery.
* Jayhawk Acceptance said it would have to seek bankruptcy law protection. Mercury Finance's unpaid debts grew, and some Olympic Financial's debt ratings were lowered.

* A shipping cartel that dominates America's $85 billion annual trade with Europe is making concessions on cargo prices and contracts that could help lower prices on a wide range of consumer products.
* Many big retailers posted healthy sales increases in January.
* Circuit City Stores and Best Buy posted sharp drops in same-store sales for January, but Tandy posted a gain.
* Germany's jobless rate soared to a record 12.2 percent in January from 10.8 percent in the prior month.
* Morgan Stanley insiders will have more than twice the stake of Dean Witter employees in the new entity formed by the two companies' merger.
* CVS has agreed to acquire Revco in a stock swap valued at more than $40 a share, people familiar with the deal say.
* Kansas City Power is close to an agreement to be acquired by hostile suitor Western Resources in a deal that could be valued at about $1.9 billion.
* Walt Disney has decided not to sell Fairchild Publications after strong interest from potential buyers.
* LVMH Moet Hennessy is close to an agreement with retail tycoon Robert Miller for LVMH to buy the remainder of DFS Group.
* Stock and bond prices traded in a narrow range, but most indexes eked out gains. The dollar rose.
* DreamWorks' stalled plans for a film studio advanced with an announcement that developer Maguire Thomas Partners has tentatively lined up $200 million in new financing.
* America Online posted a $154.8 milion net loss for its latest quarter on restructuring charges and refunds to unhappy members.
* Sotheby's Holdings suspended two employees after a British television documentary prepared to report that one of the company's traders helped smuggle a painting out of Italy.
* Allstate's fourth-quarter net rose 50 percent on improving results in its auto-insurance business and lower losses from natural disasters.
* Federal-Mogul's new chairman announced a sweeping restructuring that will reverse the strategic direction of the auto-parts maker and cut about 2,900 jobs.
* Some of Wall Street's best-known investors are packing Sotheby's Holdings auction house, bidding not for Picassos, but for profits. -- Heard on the Street.
* Bonds treaded water ahead of a monthly employment report that has Wall Street's forecasters guessing even more than usual. -- Credit Markets.
-- New York newsdesk 212-859-1610.
